title: Nonlinear Optical Probing of Ferroic-Octupolar Order Parameter in Collinear Altermagnet
authors: P. A. Usachev, R. V. Pisarev, V. V. Pavlov
abstract: Altermagnetism as a new concept in condensed matter physics is currently being thoroughly investigated. Despite the absence of macroscopic magnetization, altermagnets host a hidden spin order whose direct detection remains a challenge. Here we report on the observation of electric and magnetic dipole forbidden optical second-harmonic generation (SHG) in the altermagnet CoF$_2$ with a centrosymmetric lattice and spin order. We demonstrate that below the Néel temperature $T_N = 38$ K the SHG signal is sensitive to the ferrotype magnetic octupole $\mathbf{\mathcal{O}}^M$ which is the order parameter in the antiferromagnetic phase. By combining polarization-resolved SHG experimental data and a phenomenological symmetry analysis, we show that the altermagnetic spin structure of CoF$_2$ enables a ferroic-octupole-induced electric-quadrupolar nonlinear polarization $\mathbf{P}^{2ω} = \mathrm i\varepsilon_{0}{ }^c\mathbfχ^{(3)}(\mathbf{\mathcal{O}}^M) :\mathbf{E}^ω \nabla \mathbf{E}^ω$. The temperature dependence of SHG reveals a phase transition at $T_N$ confirming the spin origin of the observed signal. The SHG response is resonantly enhanced by a coherent three-photon process caused by the electronic $d$-$d$ transitions of the Co$^{2+}$ ion. Model calculations of SHG polarization rotational anisotropies and temperature dependencies give a reasonable agreement with experimental data, proving the disclosed nonlinear contribution. Our results establish SHG as a novel sensitive tool of ferroic-octupolar spin ordering and highlight the potential of CoF$_2$ and other altermagnets for further nonlinear optical investigations and applications.
summary: This work reports on using Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) spectroscopy as a novel, symmetry-sensitive tool to detect the ferroic-octupolar magnetic order parameter in the altermagnet $	ext{CoF}_2$. By analyzing the temperature and polarization dependence of the SHG signal relative to the Néel temperature, the authors confirm that the observed nonlinear response is directly governed by the hidden antiferromagnetic octupole moment. This establishes a powerful optical pathway for studying complex magnetic ground states.
main_problem: The study aims to develop a direct experimental method to probe the hidden ferroic-octupolar spin order parameter in altermagnets, which lack net magnetization and are invisible to standard magnetometry.
main_result: The observation of electric and magnetic dipole forbidden Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) below the Néel temperature confirms that the signal is proportional to a ferroic-octupole-induced nonlinear polarization, establishing SHG as a novel diagnostic tool for this order.
method: Nonlinear Optical Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) spectroscopy was employed, analyzing the symmetry dependence of the resulting polarization ($\mathbf{P}_{2\omega}$) relative to temperature and crystal orientation.
model_or_system: The system is the altermagnet $	ext{CoF}_2$, which exhibits a collinear Antiferromagnetic (AFM) order below $T_N = 38 	ext{ K}$. The theoretical framework models the nonlinear polarization as arising from an electric-quadrupolar term proportional to the magnetic octupole order parameter ($\mathbf{\mathcal{O}}^M$).
key_observables: SHG intensity ($I_{2\omega}$), temperature dependence of $I_{2\omega}$, and polarization anisotropy measurements across different incidence angles.
important_parameters: Néel Temperature ($T_N = 38 	ext{ K}$); the ferroic-octupole order parameter ($\mathbf{\mathcal{O}}^M$); photon energy matching three-photon resonance with $	ext{Co}^{2+}$ $d$-$d$ transitions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the total SHG signal is a sum of crystallographic and spin-induced contributions, and that interference between these two components can be neglected for robust measurement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the AFM spin order; compare polarization-dependent SHG signals above ($T>T_N$) versus below ($T<T_N$) $T_N$; and show the temperature evolution of the spin-induced component confirming its magnetic origin.
paper_structure:

why_interesting: The use of nonlinear optics (SHG) to probe higher-order magnetic multipoles ($	ext{octupole}$) is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum phases in condensed matter systems that are not captured by simple magnetization measurements.
